2) Chat vs Completions: we have a mix of short prompts (single-turn completions) and multi-turn assistant flows. When you say "chat", is the token accounting different vs completions (e.g., do system/meta messages count differently for max_tokens)?

3) Tokenization / max_tokens / stop: how do you recommend we think about max_tokens relative to input tokenization? If we set max_tokens=256 is that output-only or output+input? How robust are stop sequences across streaming responses?

4) Reranker / Embeddings: for our semantic search use-case we plan to embed docs and then rerank top-k. Does Redwood provide a reranker model or do you recommend embedding similarity + a lightweight reranker? Any benchmarks on latency for re-rank at top-10?

5) Auth: we prefer a service-account pattern for server-to-server and short-lived tokens for browser. Does the SDK handle token refresh automatically or do you recommend a proxy token endpoint?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>

Subject: Re: Acme integration: post-call recap & next steps

Alex — great questions, answered inline below at a high level. Dylan will join the tech deep-dive and can share code samples.

1) SDK / Streaming\- JS & Python SDKs both support streaming. We stream tokens as they are generated using chunked HTTP responses / SSE depending on the SDK and platform. The JS SDK exposes an async iterator so you can process partial deltas (tokens/metadata) and handle reconnects by re-issuing a request with the last good prefix (stateless resumability is limited; for strict resumability we recommend checkpointing the model's prefix locally).

2) Chat vs Completions\- "Chat" endpoints accept a messages array (system/user/assistant) and are the recommended pattern for multi-turn flows. Token accounting is the same conceptually: total tokens = input tokens + output tokens. System messages count towards input tokens. Completions endpoints accept a prompt string and are simpler for single-turn generation. If you need structured multi-role context, use chat.

3) Tokenization / max_tokens / stop\- max_tokens is output-token budget by default (the SDK enforces output cap), but total token count must fit model context window (input + max_tokens <= model_context). We recommend computing tokens client-side using our tokenizer utilities in the SDK to validate before sending. Stop sequences are applied by the model and are generally honored; during streaming you may receive a final partial chunk that contains the stop string — SDKs will emit that chunk and then close the stream. If you need strict truncation semantics, post-process the final text for stop markers.

4) Reranker / Embeddings\- Two recommended patterns: a) embedding similarity (FAISS or managed vector DB) -> top-K, then a lightweight learned reranker (small cross-encoder) for final ordering; or b) use a tuned reranker model as a second-stage model in Redwood (higher latency but better precision). For top-10 rerank we often see sub-200ms median on our Dedicated clusters for optimized configs; exact numbers depend on model choice and hardware.

5) Auth\- Service-account tokens + short-lived exchange is our recommended production pattern. For browser calls we recommend sending requests to a short-lived proxy token endpoint you run (so you never embed long-lived keys in the client). The SDK can accept token refresh callbacks; we don't automatically mint user tokens for you. The attached auth guide shows examples for both flows.

Proposed follow-up: Mon May 30 09:00 PT for a 45 minute tech session (Dylan + infra). Confirm and we'll send calendar invite.

Best,

Marissa

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>

Marissa / Alex — attached are the artifacts I prepared: streaming-example.js (small JS sample using the Redwood SDK async iterator), routing-policy.md (short doc with routing recommendations), and a tiny benchmark note for top-10 rerank on our Dedicated cluster. Key points:

- Streaming: the JS example uses client.chat.stream() which yields partial chunks with token text + delta role + generation metadata. We signal finalization when chunk.finished==true; stop sequences are often delivered in the last chunk and we recommend a final sanitize step to trim trailing stop tokens.

- Resumability: true resumability requires model-side state; our pragmatic recommendation is local checkpointing of the generated prefix and re-issuing the request if a reconnect happens (best-effort).

- Routing: prefer a quantized 8-bit variant for bulk low-sensitivity calls (~30-40% cost savings) and route to the FP16/high-accuracy model for quality-critical flows. Use per-route policies in the config with canary % and fallback to higher tier on failures. Example policy attached in routing-policy.md.

- Rerank perf: our small internal benchmark (on Dedicated A100-equivalent) shows p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 420ms for a cross-encoder reranker on top-10. Your mileage will vary based on model and infra.

I've attached the files: streaming-example.js, routing-policy.md, rerank-bench.md

If Mon May 30 09:00 PT still works for you Alex, I can demo the streaming example live.

Thanks,
